description: What to Know Before (and After) You Hire an Advisor (w/ Matthew Taylor) | #427

turns.en: Welcome to episode 427 of the Rational Reminder Podcast. I'm Ben Felix, Chief Investment Officer at PWL Capital. And I'm Cameron Passmore, Chief Executive Officer at PWL Capital.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听《Rational Reminder》播客第 427 期。我是 Ben Felix，PWL Capital 的首席投资官 (Chief Investment Officer)。我是 Cameron Passmore，PWL Capital 的首席执行官 (Chief Executive Officer)。

turns.en: Today we're joined by Matthew Taylor, a litigation lawyer with SOTO's class action in Toronto who represents retail investors and pension funds and securities class actions. He also works with Harold Geller, who's a guest on this podcast in episode 236.
turns.zh: 今天我们请到的嘉宾是 Matthew Taylor，他是多伦多 Sotos 律师事务所集体诉讼团队的诉讼律师，代表散户投资者和养老基金参与证券集体诉讼 (securities class actions)。他还和 Harold Geller 共事，Harold 曾是我们的嘉宾，在第 236 期。

turns.en: And today we discuss what makes a successful negligence claim against an advisor, the fiduciary standard in Canada, and what retail investors need to know about private equity and influencers.
turns.zh: 今天我们要讨论：什么样的疏忽索赔 (negligence claim) 才有可能成功告倒一位顾问、加拿大的受托人标准 (fiduciary standard)，以及散户投资者需要了解哪些关于私募股权 (private equity) 和网络博主 (influencer) 的事。

turns.en: And stick around to the end to hear our thoughts on the conversation. But for now, let's get into the conversation with Matthew Taylor. Matthew Taylor, welcome to the Rational Reminder Podcast. Thank you for having me.

turns.zh: 做不了。所以你要尽早评估自己有没有法律救济。另外也有一些免费资源可以探索，比如 Osgoode 投资者保护诊所 (Osgoode Investor Protection Clinic)，那里的工作非常出色——那是学生运营的，挂队的指导律师——我们也参与帮助那些请不起律师、打不起完整官司的人拿到了一定程度的赔偿，这总比什么都没有强。

turns.en: better than nothing. What do you think financial advisors should be doing to assess the risk tolerance of their clients? An important piece or a conversation that seems like isn't happening as much as it should, would be risk capacity with people as well.
turns.zh: 你觉得财务顾问在评估客户的风险偏好 (risk tolerance) 方面应该做些什么？我觉得有一块重要的、但现在似乎谈得不够的对话，是风险承受能力 (risk capacity)。

turns.en: I think anything that you can do to explore this, I think talking about scenarios can be a really good one because everybody has that conversation, I think with somebody that comes in, they're like, yeah, I have great risk tolerance. I want to do some gambling, but if you talk to them, okay, what happens if you lose your job? What if your company answers into bankruptcy? Or how would affect your life if all of this money was gone? Or if it was completely locked up in some liquid
turns.zh: 我认为凡是能帮你探究这件事的方法都值得做。谈情景是个非常好的方法。我想每个人都会碰到那种客户：'没错，我风险偏好很高，我就想赌一把。'但如果你跟他聊：要是你失业了怎么办？要是你所在的公司申请破产了怎么办？如果这些钱全没了，或者被完全锁在某个非流动基金里，会如何影响你的生活？然后他们开始谈论所有这些可怕的人生后果，

turns.en: fund and they all started talking about all these horrible life consequences that they could have? And as they're talking through that, okay, maybe my risk tolerance is in where I thought it was.
turns.zh: 一边说一边就会意识到：好吧，也许我的风险偏好并不像我以为的那么高。

turns.en: So I think exploring in a more concrete way is something that people will respond to a bit better, I believe. We have a risk tolerance questionnaire that we do with clients and we also have a risk capacity questionnaire and has six questions. Do you have a positive net worth?
turns.zh: 所以我觉得，用更具体的方式来探究，人们会更能接受。我们公司有一个用于客户的风险偏好问卷，我们还有一个风险承受能力问卷，有六个问题：你的净资产是否为正？

turns.en: Do you have sufficient liquidity to cover three to six months of living expenses? Do you have stable employment or pension income? Are you currently withdrawing more than 3% from your investments annually? Do you have adequate life and disability insurance?
turns.zh: 你有足够的流动性覆盖三到六个月的生活开支吗？你有稳定的工作或养老金收入吗？你目前每年从投资中提取的比例是否超过 3%？你有充足的人寿保险和失能保险吗？

turns.en: And do you anticipate making a withdrawal of greater than 10% from your long-term portfolio? If yes, what is the expected time horizon for the withdrawals and it ranges from less than a year to more than 10 years? That is a much more robust process. I think a lot of other places have many other firms, so I think that will certainly serve your clients well. And the fact that there's a discussion happening about risk capacity versus tolerance at all,
turns.zh: 以及你是否预期会从长期组合中取出超过 10% 的款项？如果是，预计的取款时间跨度是多长——选项从不到一年到十年以上不等？这可是一套扎实得多的流程。我想其他很多机构也有类似机制，所以我相信这一定能很好地服务你们的客户。而且，居然能有一场关于风险承受能力与风险偏好的讨论这件事本身——

turns.en: there are many, many calls live with people where they're not aware that those are two separate concepts. It's just not part of the discussion that they've ever had.
turns.zh: 我接触过的很多人根本不知道这是两个不同的概念，他们的对话里从来就没有这个话题。

turns.en: Yeah, that's wild. You mentioned earlier that you've got a biased sample because people come to you after something has gone wrong. So we're kind of acknowledging that your sample is biased.
turns.zh: 是啊，太离谱了。你前面说过你的样本是有偏差的，因为人们都是出了事之后才来找你。所以我们算是承认了样本偏差。

turns.en: How well do you think investors, retail investors, understand risk, probably speaking when it comes to investing? I would say it's generally pretty poor overall. I think that there are a lot of aspects of risk that aren't discussed where people don't have an understanding of the general public.
turns.zh: 你怎么看投资者——散户投资者——对风险的理解程度，大概地说，在投资这件事上？我觉得总体来说相当差。风险的很多维度根本没有被讨论，公众对这些没有概念。

turns.en: I think people essentially think of the risk of the loss of their invested capital and they think this asset class has more or less risk. And they're not thinking about different forms of risk, like liquidity risk is something that I don't think people give much consideration to.
turns.zh: 我认为人们基本上把风险等同于投资本金的亏损，觉得这个资产类别风险高一点、那个低一点。他们不会去想不同形式的风险。比如流动性风险 (liquidity risk)，我觉得人们很少认真考虑。

turns.en: Sequence of return risk or withdrawal risk, those forms of risk, I think that they're just completely off of most people's radars. And they just have this very rudimentary understanding of what investment risk is or what kinds of financial risks they face. So I believe the average person that's coming in looking for advice, they're probably coming in with extremely limited knowledge of what risk actually means or the ways that it can manifest. And again, in your experience,
turns.zh: 还有回报序列风险 (sequence of returns risk)、提取风险 (withdrawal risk) 这些形式的风险，我觉得完全不在大多数人的雷达上。他们对投资风险是什么、自己面临哪些财务风险的理解非常初级。所以我相信，一般的普通人来寻求建议时，对风险到底意味着什么、风险会如何显现，几乎是知之甚少的。那么以你的经验，

turns.en: Matthew, how well do financial advisors understand risk? I think that's much more variable. That certainly runs the range. There are people that are extremely sophisticated and have an excellent understanding of it. They have processes like you've been describing to educate their clients and have those conversations. And I've certainly met a lot of people like that and I learned a great deal from them. So I always appreciate that. I think there are also people there at the other
turns.zh: Matthew，财务顾问对风险的理解程度如何？我觉得这就千差万别了，确实是全光谱都有。有些人极其老练，对风险理解得很透彻，他们有你们描述的这种流程来教育客户、开展这些对话。我确实见过很多这样的人，也从他们身上学到很多，我一直很感激这一点。但也有些人在光谱的另一端，

turns.en: end of the spectrum who have probably not much greater an understanding than the people that they're advising. Frankly, the barrier to entry dent, the industry is quite low. The licensing process as an educational component, I wouldn't say it's a super robust educational component. I think for some of the licenses, my understanding is it's still basically a multiple choice test.
turns.zh: 他们的理解恐怕跟他们的客户差不了多少。坦白讲，这个行业的准入门槛相当低。考取牌照过程中的教育部分，我不敢说是多么扎实的教育。据我了解，有几个牌照基本上至今还是多选题考试。

turns.en: There's a greater degree of variability here. There are some excellent, excellent people that have a very strong understanding of it. And there are going to be people who are in between as well.
turns.zh: 这里的差异性要大得多。有些非常优秀的人对风险有很深的理解，也会有介于两者之间的人。

turns.en: I remember when I did my licenses initially, which was just a mutual funds license and an insurance license, I look back on what I knew then and it's terrifying that I was licensed to give advice. And then the crazier part is that most of your education comes from the firm that you're with and most of the education within firms often comes from product providers who are brought in for lunch and learns or whatever. And so all your education is coming from folks who
turns.zh: 我记得我刚考牌照那会儿，只考了共同基金牌照和保险牌照。回头看当时自己懂的那点东西，真庆幸自己居然被发牌可以给别人提供建议。更夸张的是，你大部分的学习来自你所在的公司，而公司内部的很多培训又来自产品供应商——他们被请来做午餐分享会 (lunch and learn) 之类。所以你所有的教育都来自那些

turns.en: are selling you a product, which you're then turning around and selling to your clients. But if there's no independent education happening, you can get a pretty skewed view of how things work and what risk is. People gravitate a lot of the time towards doing the bare minimum, unfortunately. And if the bare minimum that you're firm is learning about their product shelf or the hearing from the product, people, what they're saying, that's going to be
turns.zh: 卖产品给你的人，然后你再转头把这些产品卖给客户。如果没有独立的教育来源，你对世界如何运作、风险是什么的理解就会相当偏。人们很多时候会倾向于只做最低限度的事，很不幸。如果你的最低限度就是了解你们公司的产品货架，或者听产品方的人怎么说，那这至少就是

turns.en: a big part of why at least some of the advisors are going to be absorbing and that's going to be flowing through to the advice that they provide people. So I'm working with Harold Geller, who I understand was a guest on the past, and he likes to tell a story about how he got, I think, his mutual fund license, maybe it was the Canadian security scores like fresh out of high school, went essentially absolutely nothing. There are people out there that does their background
turns.zh: 一部分顾问吸收信息的方式，并且会直接流入他们给出的建议。所以我现在和 Harold Geller 共事，据我所知他也上过你们这个播客。他喜欢讲他当年是怎么拿到牌照的——我想是共同基金牌照，也许就是 Canadian Securities Course (CSC)——刚高中毕业就去考了，脑子里基本上什么都没有。确实有人以这样的背景进入这个行业。但这不意味着他们永远停留在那个教育水平，

turns.en: coming into this space and that doesn't mean that they're going to remain at that level of education forever. Lots of people go on to continue to learn and improve and I'm sure provide an excellent service to their client, but there are also people who are not going to learn much more and they're not going to make a lot of effort to improve from that place.
turns.zh: 很多人后来不断学习、不断进步，我相信他们为客户提供了出色的服务。但也确实有人不会再多学什么，也不会花多大力气从那个起点去改进。

turns.en: The bar is low. The entry level to be licensed and qualified to give advice, it's not like being a lawyer where you can be pretty sure people have gone through pretty rigorous education. It's kind of interesting that you say that because what you were saying, I think a lot of it is similar to law. The barrier to entry is higher in going to law school, but in terms of actually learning out of practice law competently,
turns.zh: 门槛就是这么低。拿到牌照、有资格提供建议的入门水平，不像当律师那样，你可以相当确定人们接受过相当严格的教育。你说这个挺有意思——我觉得法律行业在很多方面也类似。进法学院的门槛更高，但要说真正学会胜任地执业，

turns.en: you mostly give that for your firm and the people that you work with and that can be extremely variable. It's not like medicine where you're licensed to practice in a particular area.
turns.zh: 你主要还是从你所在的律所和共事的人那里学，而那可以差异极大。不像医学，你被发牌执业的方向是限定的。

turns.en: Your law degree, you get called to the bar, you can theoretically try and take on any kind of mandate at that point, even if it would be terrifyingly complex and you don't have the experience. There are some similarities there, I think. Oh, that's very interesting. What are the conditions for financial advisors that imply a fiduciary duty in Canada? I wish that this was a simpler question to answer, and unfortunately, it can be difficult for people going in to know
turns.zh: 法律学位拿到、被宣告律师资格 (called to the bar) 之后，理论上你可以尝试接任何类型的委托，哪怕它复杂得吓人而你毫无经验。我觉得有些地方是相似的。哦，这很有意思。在加拿大，哪些情形会让财务顾问隐含受托义务 (fiduciary duty)？我希望这个问题能简单点，但不幸的是，人们在进入关系时很难知道自己

turns.en: if they're dealing with a fiduciary or not. Generally speaking, in the context of people who are providing professional advice, there's five factors that are going to drive the analysis, and a lot of them are related to what we've been talking about already. The biggest one is vulnerability, and vulnerability can take a lot of different forms. It can be that language barrier that we were talking about before. It might be their very rudimentary level of investment knowledge.
turns.zh: 面对的是不是受托人。一般来说，在提供专业建议的情境中，有五个因素会主导分析，其中很多我们已经聊过了。最大的是脆弱性 (vulnerability)，它可以有很多表现形式：就是我们之前说的语言障碍，可能是非常初级的投资知识水平，

turns.en: It might be a lack of education or limited professional experience that would be relevant. Anything that's going to heighten that asymmetry that I mentioned before between the professional advisor and the client, the second factor the courts will look to is the degree of trust.
turns.zh: 可能是教育程度的欠缺，或者相关专业经验有限——凡是会加大专业人士与客户之间那道不对称的都算。法院会看的第二个因素是信任的程度 (degree of trust)。

turns.en: If somebody actually was completely trusting and reliant on their advisor, that's going to strongly militate towards it being a fiduciary relationship. A related piece would be reliance.
turns.zh: 如果一个人完全信任、完全依赖自己的顾问，那会非常有力地指向受托关系的成立。相关的另一块是依赖 (reliance)。

turns.en: If somebody has been following their advisor's advice basically 100% of the time, relying completely on them, that's going to push more out towards the fiduciary and the things, versus somebody who may follow the advice some of the time, but not all the time, or might disregard the advice most of the time. That person is going to have a much harder time having a court say that was a fiduciary relationship that you were in. Discretion
turns.zh: 如果某人基本上 100% 听从顾问的建议、完全依赖对方，那会更靠近受托关系。而另一些人有的时间听、有的时间不听，或者大多数时候干脆无视建议，这种人要让法院认定'那是一段受托关系'就难得多。自由裁量权 (discretion)

turns.en: is one of the key hallmarks. So if you've got a discretionary account, that's going to be one of the strongest indicators. But it's not just what the paperwork says, because you can find many instances of civil lawsuits or regulatory proceedings, or non-discretionary accounts have been treated as discretionary, or discretionary accounts have actually been treated more like an order execution account where the client is directing what's happening.
turns.zh: 是最核心的标志之一。如果你有一个全权委托账户 (discretionary account)，那就是最强的指标之一。但这不只看纸面文件，因为在很多民事官司或监管程序里，你会看到非全权账户实际上被当成了全权账户操作；也有全权账户实际上被当成了下单执行账户 (order execution account)，由客户在指挥一切。

turns.en: So the court's going to look at the reality of the situation, not just what it says on the account statement. The last indicator is if there are professional rules or codes of conduct, or if they're a member of some form of a professional organization that says that follows a fiduciary standard, or adopts some of those other indicia of a fiduciary relationship as part of the mandate for the organization, and somebody advertises themselves as being part of that organization,
turns.zh: 所以法院看的是实际情况，不是对账单上写了什么。最后一个指标是：如果有职业规则或行为准则，或者他是某个职业组织的成员，而该组织奉行受托人标准、把受托关系的其他特征写进了组织的职责，而这个人又对外宣传自己是那个组织的成员、

turns.en: meeting those standards, the court is going to hold them to that. Yeah, that one I find so interesting that if you say you're a fiduciary, you're likely to be held to that standard. It's an important factor. And unfortunately, there are situations where people will say that it's not necessarily in writing, and then you find yourself in the he said she said kind of thing, and we're talking about the evidence relating to it. But if somebody clearly is
turns.zh: 符合那些标准，法院就会按这个标准要求他。嗯，我觉得有意思的正是这一点：如果你说自己是受托人，你就很可能被按那个标准来衡量。这是个重要因素。遗憾的是，有些情况下只是口头说、没有落在纸上，于是你又回到了各说各话，而我们一直在谈证据问题。但如果有人明显地

turns.en: advertising themselves as such, that's going to be a much stronger indicator that they are. Interesting. We are at PWL discretionary portfolio managers, and we go through a third-party certification. We're audited, and this third party called CFEX, the Center for Fiduciary Excellence, they certify us as acting as fiduciaries, which we then present to clients. So between those two things, it's highly likely we would be held to a fiduciary standard if we were in court.
turns.zh: 把自己宣传成受托人，那就会是一个强得多的指标。有意思。我们是 PWL，全权委托组合管理公司，我们接受第三方认证。我们被审计，有一个叫 CFEX 的第三方——信托卓越中心 (Center for Fiduciary Excellence)——认证我们确实以受托人身份行事，然后我们会把认证展示给客户。所以这两条加起来，如果在法庭上，我们被按受托人标准要求的可能性非常高。

turns.en: I think that's right. That would be very powerful evidence that you are a fiduciary, and if people want to be really explicit, they can put it in their contracts too. Like you can contractually create a fiduciary relationship. There's nothing that prevents people from doing that. I personally haven't encountered that, but theoretically a possibility.
turns.zh: 我认为没错。那会是非常有力的受托人证据。如果有人想做得更明确，他们还可以写进合同：你完全可以在合同上创设一个受托关系，没有什么妨碍这么做。我个人还没遇到过，但理论上是可行的。

turns.en: Interesting. Oh, and I guess we also have, most of our advisors are CFA, CIM, or CFP, and often some combination of those things, and all of those have their own standards and codes of ethics, which typically promote a best interest standard.
turns.zh: 有意思。对了，我想我们大多数顾问都持有 CFA、CIM 或 CFP，常常是几个的组合，而这些资格各自都有标准和道德守则，通常都倡导最佳利益标准 (best interest standard)。

turns.en: That's a big one. So I have been involved in lawsuits suing people who are CFA charter holders, and that's absolutely something that we relied on in terms of pushing that lawsuit ahead and arguing the fiduciary standard reply. For context for people for why we care about this, how does legally acceptable advice differ between an advisor who is held to a fiduciary standard and one who's held to a suitability standard? So the best interest standard is a big piece of it.
turns.zh: 这一点很重要。所以我参与过起诉 CFA 持证人的官司，我们确实依赖了这一点来推进诉讼、主张适用受托人标准。给听众一个背景——我们为什么在乎这件事：被要求遵守受托标准的顾问，和被要求只遵守适当性标准 (suitability standard) 的顾问，法律上可接受的建议有何不同？最佳利益标准是其中很大一块。

turns.en: Fiduciary, I believe it's a Latin word. It's a word that basically means trust. So we're talking about a trust relationship, and for context, the normal sort of negligence relationship is you need to meet a standard of care in this context. That's suitability.
turns.zh: Fiduciary 这个词我想是拉丁语，基本含义就是信托 (trust)。所以我们说的是一种信任关系。作为参照，通常的疏忽责任关系，你需要达到的是注意义务标准 (standard of care)，在这个语境里就是适当性。

turns.en: Inherent and suitability is not a best interest standard. It's that you're making an appropriate recommendation based on the person's needs and the products that you're suggesting to them.
turns.zh: 适当性本身并不是最佳利益标准。它只是说，你基于这个人的需求和产品，做出了一个合适的推荐。

turns.en: If you have a best interest standard, or if you are held to a fiduciary standard, there's some other stuff that attaches to that. You need to make disclosure.
turns.zh: 如果你有最佳利益标准，或者你被要求遵守受托人标准，那还有别的东西随之而来。你需要披露——

turns.en: You need to make disclosure of any kind of conflict of interest, and if there is one, then you need informed consent from the person to accept that conflict, basically, and you need to make recommendations that are based on their best interests and aren't informed by your own. Theoretically, you can make suitable recommendations that result in higher compensation to you, or there might be some other benefit flowing to you,
turns.zh: 你需要披露任何类型的利益冲突；如果存在冲突，你还得获得客户对该冲突的知情同意 (informed consent)。基本上，你得基于客户的最佳利益给建议，而不是受你自己利益的左右。理论上，你可以给出适当但让你自己拿更高佣金、或让你有其他好处的建议，

turns.en: and you don't necessarily have to disclose that either. It wouldn't be inherently unsuitable. There might be other things that would flow from that, but just taking that one piece in the abstract, that's one way that it can differ. So given that how important should obtaining a fiduciary relationship be from the client's perspective? Having from the client perspective, there's no drawback. I believe that a lot of people when they're seeking out advice,
turns.zh: 而且你未必需要披露这一点，它也不必然是不适当的。可能有其他衍生问题，但就单拿这一点抽象地讲，这就是两者的区别之一。既然这样，从客户的角度看，争取受托关系应该有多重要？从客户的角度，没有任何坏处。我相信大多数人在寻求建议时，

turns.en: they probably have an expectation that those kinds of things would be disclosed to them, or there would be a discussion about it. My sense, when I speak to most people, is that they believe that that's something that must, should, or is happening when the reality can be a little bit different. A lot of other professional advisors are automatically fiduciaries. Doctors are fiduciaries.
turns.zh: 都默认这类信息会向他们披露，或者至少会讨论。我跟大多数人聊下来的感觉是，他们认为这件事一定是、应该是、或者已经在发生了，但现实可能不一样。很多其他专业人士自动就是受托人：医生是受托人，

turns.en: Lawyers are fiduciaries. There's a whole bunch of other categories where that does automatically attach. But when we're in the world of financial and investment advice, it's not something that's as automatic as that, whether people believe it or not. From the client perspective, there aren't really any drawbacks. It can make proving legal claims easier, and it might also provide some level of assurance that they know that the person they're dealing with holds themselves to this
turns.zh: 律师是受托人。还有一大类职业，受托义务自动就附着上去。可一旦进入财务和投资建议的世界，这件事并不像人们想象的那么自动。从客户的角度看，真的没什么坏处。它可以让法律索赔更容易证明，也可能给客户某种安心：知道跟自己打交道的人是在以更高的标准

turns.en: heightened standard. So I know it can be difficult to identify, and maybe depending on the geographic area you're in, if you want to work with somebody in person, the pool might be more limited. So I don't know that it should be the only deciding factor, but all else being equal. There's absolutely no drawback from the client perspective, and I would think that you would always want a fiduciary over a non-fiduciary. Could be higher minimums too. Absolutely. So there could be a lot of other
turns.zh: 要求自己。我知道要识别可能不容易，而且取决于你所在的地区，如果你想跟本地的人当面合作，池子可能更窄。所以它不一定该是唯一的决定因素，但在其他条件相同的情况下，从客户角度看完全没有坏处，我觉得你永远应该选受托人而不是非受托人。受托顾问的最低投资门槛可能也更高。没错，可能有很多其他原因

turns.en: reasons why it doesn't happen, or why it's not available to somebody. We touched on some of the characteristics, but if an investor is looking for a fiduciary, how can they identify them? What should they be looking for? I think realistically, the strongest thing that they can do is look for association with an organization that has some of the standards you were talking about before, something like the fiduciary pledge the F-PAC has. That pledge pretty explicitly incorporates a lot
turns.zh: 导致这事没成或无法获得。我们聊过一些特征了，但如果一个投资者想找受托人，他们怎么识别？应该看什么？我觉得现实一点，最有力的是看与某个有标准的组织的关联，比如你刚才提到的 FPAC 的受托人承诺 (fiduciary pledge)。那个承诺相当明确地包含了

turns.en: of the elements we were talking about in that five-par analysis that the courts undergo. It matches up pretty closely with that. I think the first part of the F-PAC pledge is to put the needs of the client first ahead of the advisor's own needs. So that's that best interest standard pretty explicitly incorporated there. And then I believe they also explicitly says that there is a duty of loyalty that attaches to it. Again, that's one of those core issues of a fiduciary
turns.zh: 我们说过的法院五因素分析里的那些要素，与它几乎一一对应。我想 FPAC 承诺的第一部分是：把客户的需求放在顾问自身利益之前。这就把最佳利益标准相当明确地写进去了。然后我相信它还明确说附带忠实义务 (duty of loyalty)，那也是受托关系

turns.en: relationship and minimizing conflicts of interest as another and full and transparent disclosure. So pretty explicitly built into that pledge, which is publicly available. Everybody can see it, and I think people advertise their affiliation with F-PAC. So that would be a pretty strong indicator if somebody was looking for a fiduciary specifically. For listeners, F-PAC is an industry association, the Financial Planning Association of Canada. I'm a member. I don't know how many
turns.zh: 的核心之一；再加上把利益冲突降到最低，以及完整、透明的披露。所以这些都相当明确地写在那个公开可查的承诺里，而且我看到有人宣传自己的 FPAC 会员身份。如果有人专门要找受托人，那就是个相当强的指标。给听众补充一下，FPAC 是一个行业组织，Financial Planning Association of Canada。我是会员，我不知道 PWL 还有多少同事

turns.en: other folks at PWLR, but good organization. What types of issues in financial markets typically result in class action lawsuits? So class actions tend to have different components on what we've been talking about. And just to back up a little bit, most of what we've been talking about before would be a fairly standard sort of lawsuit. One client, one or two defendants, the firm and the advisor. You can also group people together. You might have 20 clients of one person,
turns.zh: 是会员，不过那是个好组织。哪些类型的金融市场问题通常会引发集体诉讼 (class action)？集体诉讼跟我们之前聊的东西不太一样。先往后退一步：我们前面讲的大多是相当普通的诉讼：一个客户，一到两个被告——公司和顾问本人。你也可以把人组团：比如同一个人的 20 个客户

turns.en: and they all come together and they suit together. That's not a class action. That's just a group action. A group of people all deciding to retain one lawyer and suit together to take advantage of economies of scale. A class action is an entirely different procedure where you can have one person come forward, a single person that is seeking to represent the interests of everybody who's similar to them. It can be thousands of people. It could be hundreds,
turns.zh: 凑在一起、一起起诉。那不是集体诉讼，那只是联合诉讼 (group action)：一群人决定共同委托一个律师、一起打官司以享受规模效应。集体诉讼则完全是另一种程序：一个人可以站出来，寻求代表所有跟他处境相似的人，可以是几千人，可以是几百人、

turns.en: tens of thousands. There have been a few cases where it would probably affect millions of people if it was a price fixing conspiracy, something of that nature. As a result, there's really pretty minimal involvement from anybody else who's affected. And a group action need to go through all the process of litigation. You need to retain a lawyer. You need to be examined under oath. You need to exchange your documents. It's quite a big process to engage in. It comes with a lot of stress
turns.zh: 几万人。有一些案件，如果是价格操纵 (price fixing) 阴谋之类的，影响的人可能以百万计。所以实际上其他受影响者的参与微乎其微。而联合诉讼要走完诉讼的全部流程：你得请律师，你得接受宣誓讯问 (examined under oath)，你们得交换文件。这个过程相当庞大，

turns.en: and anxiety. And if you lose, you're exposed to adverse costs. You might need to pay some amount of the defendant's legal fees. So there's a very real financial downside. In a class action where you have this one person coming forward, they're effectively always indemnified. The lawyer representing them will agree to pay for that so that there isn't this enormous risk to that individual. And the people who are named on the lawsuit, they don't have any kind of exposure at all until the point
turns.zh: 伴随大量压力和焦虑。而且如果输了，你面临不利费用 (adverse costs)，可能需要赔付被告的部分律师费，所以有实实在在的财务下行风险。而在集体诉讼里，那个站出来的人基本上总是被兜底的：代理律师会同意承担这笔费用，使这个人不至于独自面对巨大风险。诉讼文书上列名的人，在真正需要参与诉讼之前没有任何风险敞口。

turns.en: that they need to participate in the lawsuit. Because of the fact that we're dealing with such a different procedure, you can only do certain kinds of cases as class actions. You can't deal with every kind of legal dispute through that procedure because it sort of falls apart.
turns.zh: 正因为程序如此不同，你只能把某些类型的案件做成集体诉讼。不是所有法律纠纷都能用这个程序，它在某些场景下会失灵。

turns.en: You need the court's permission to proceed with a class action because it can affect the rights of people who aren't before the court. You can just file it and say, this is a class action grape.
turns.zh: 你需要法院的许可才能推进集体诉讼，因为它会影响未出庭者的权利。你不能随便递个文件说一句'这是集体诉讼'就完了。

turns.en: It needs to be approved by the court. And part of that approval process is, are there actually common issues between all of the people who are affected by this lawsuit? And if we're dealing with something like the advisor relationship, if you're dealing with somebody that needs to go through suitability analysis, that's an inherently individualized analysis. There's an individual conversation that needs to happen between the advisor and the client. There's individual advice
turns.zh: 它需要法院批准。批准程序的一部分是：所有受这场诉讼影响的人之间，是否真的存在共同争点 (common issues)？如果我们处理的是顾问关系这类需要逐一做适当性分析的东西——那天生就是个体化的分析，需要顾问与客户之间一对一的对话，存在个体化的建议，

turns.en: being given if things are going accordingly. So it doesn't make sense for those to be legated as class actions. What you are dealing with when you're in the world of a class action where there's these common problems are two major buckets of claims. They're disclosure issues with publicly listed companies. Pick whatever your favorite TSX company is. If they're failing to make disclosure, if they're treating a financial state of affairs, if there's some large operational issue,
turns.zh: 一切正常运转时更是如此。所以这些案子不适合按集体诉讼来处理。而集体诉讼的世界里，真正存在共同问题的主要是两大类索赔。一是上市公司的披露问题 (disclosure)。随便挑你最喜欢的一家 TSX 公司：如果他们没能做到披露——财务状况陈述不实、存在重大运营问题——

turns.en: you can't work in this space in Canada without having at some point a mining claim. So if you're dealing with a junior mining company that's misrepresenting the amount of gold that they have or whether or not their operations are in compliance with their environmental permits that comes to light, the bottom falls over, there's a huge decline in share price, that type of claim is very amenable to class action litigation and basically only happens
turns.zh: 在加拿大做这一行，你迟早会碰到矿业标的 (mining claim)。如果一家初级矿业公司虚报黄金储量，或者隐瞒其运营不符合环境许可要求，之后东窗事发，股价崩盘，这种索赔就非常适合集体诉讼，而且基本上只能通过集体诉讼来实现。第二类是针对资产管理人的索赔，涉及他们如何管理资产：比如针对共同基金经理、ETF 经理，

turns.en: through class action litigation. The second genre would be claims against asset managers relating to how they've managed the assets. So you might have claims against mutual fund managers, ETF managers based on how they've been charging fees, based on whether or not the investments of their funds are holding actually match up with what they've told their investors are going to be under the hood, those types of things because it's not this individualized analysis. Everybody is buying
turns.zh: 基于他们如何收费，基于基金实际持仓是否兑现了他们向投资人承诺的底层资产。这类案件之所以更适合集体认定 (class determination)，是因为它不是个体化分析——每个人买那支共同基金或那个 ETF，

turns.en: that mutual fund or that ETF based on what they believe the investment approach is that wins itself much better to class determination. I think asset managers as opposed to financial advisors are held to a stricter or to a more explicit fiduciary standard. Is that right?
turns.zh: 都是基于他们相信的那套投资方法。我觉得资产管理人——相比财务顾问——被要求遵守更严格、或者更明确的受托标准，是这样吗？

turns.en: Yes. So the Securities Act actually explicitly contains a fiduciary standard attaching to certain kinds of asset managers. So that's literally written into a statute. I believe that's the case in every province. It's certainly the case in Ontario.
turns.zh: 对。《证券法》(Securities Act) 的成文法里明确规定某些类型的资产管理人负有受托义务。这是白纸黑字写进法条的。我相信每个省都是如此，安大略省肯定是。

turns.en: What are some of the signs that a class action is likely to be successful? So class actions are different in a few other respects and we're talking more about the business perspective than necessarily the strictly legal, but these are very large, complex pieces of litigation. If you look at the lawyers who are willing to run them, it's a relatively small group of firms compared to a lot of other areas of law.
turns.zh: 一个集体诉讼可能成功的迹象有哪些？集体诉讼在其他几个方面也不一样。我们更多是从商业角度讲，而不完全是严格从法律角度。这些是非常庞大、复杂的诉讼。你看愿意接这类案子的律所，跟法律的其他领域相比只是相对少数几家。

turns.en: And there are some firms that will dabble. They might do one or two, but most of them are run by specialists and the specialists are fairly few and far between. So the involvement of one of these specialist firms in and of itself is an indicator because they're taking their time, they're taking their capital and they're thinking this is a good investment of their time in capital versus something else that they might be doing. And they're willing to take that significant
turns.zh: 有些律所偶尔试水一两个，但绝大多数由专业所操盘，而专业所也屈指可数。所以其中一家专业所的参与本身就是一个指标，因为他们投入的是自己的时间和资本，认定这是比他们本可以做的其他事情更好的时间和资本投向。他们也愿意承担我

turns.en: downside risk that I mentioned before because the lawyers are the ones who are going to be on the hook if things go wrong and the lawsuit is lost. So if you've got the involvement of a repeatable firm that's had a great degree of success, if they've had good results and other similar claims, that's a pretty strong indicator. With a dabble or a firm that doesn't do much of these, that gives you less information. Some of those are very well run. I'm not saying that
turns.zh: 前面提到的那种重大下行风险——因为一旦事情搞砸、官司打输，被追责掏钱的是律师。所以如果你遇到一家反复做这类案子、战绩很好的律所——他们在类似索赔中有过漂亮结果——那是个很强的指标。偶尔试水的或者做得不多的律所给你的信息就少一些。我不是说

turns.en: only specialist firms can do these lawsuits. It's just much harder to evaluate. Class actions are large enough and expensive enough. So there's actually a market for funding.
turns.zh: 只有专业所才能做这些诉讼，只是更难评估。集体诉讼的体量和成本之大，催生了一个真正的诉讼融资 (litigation funding) 市场。

turns.en: There are third-party funders and these are, in some cases, investment firms. They're essentially buying a piece of the litigation and they're willing to take on the risk of the adverse cost or they're willing to put up millions of dollars to fund the expert fees and what you need to actually get one of these things across the finish line. They keep pushing it towards trial or a meaningful settlement. So that's giving you another layer of somebody with a lot of specialized
turns.zh: 存在第三方出资人 (third-party funder)，其中有些本身就是投资公司。他们本质上是在买下诉讼的一部分份额，愿意承担不利费用 (adverse cost) 的风险，或者愿意掏出几百万美元来支付专家费用——让这类案件真正跑到终点线所需的一切。他们推着案件朝审判或有意义的和解前进。这就又给了你一层：一位拥有大量专业

turns.en: expertise taking a look at this and saying, I'm willing to risk my capital on this. So I think if you've got a funded claim, that gives you a bit more confidence as well that there are more people that think that this is something that's going to have some degree of success. Beyond those factors, which are really more business considerations, but I think they give some information, there are certain other things that will suggest this has got some merit or it's going
turns.zh: 知识的人看过之后说：我愿意把我的资本押上去。所以我觉得，如果一个索赔背后有出资，你会更有信心：说明又有更多人认为它有相当的胜算。除了这些因素——它们其实更多是商业考量，但我认为确实能传递信息——还有一些别的东西会表明案子有其道理、

turns.en: to have a good result. If there's a regulatory proceeding, if there's a prosecution by a Provincial Securities Commission, let's say, then again, you've got another sophisticated actor saying something went wrong here. We need to take a look at that. And another piece of it is I might give you a source of evidence or information. Some of that might become public and that might be something that you can rely upon if you're representing a class of people. Another strong indicator can be
turns.zh: 会有好结果。如果有监管程序，如果有省级证券委员会提起的执法行动——比方说——那又是一位精通此道的参与者表示：这里出了问题，我们得看看。还有一点是，这可能会给你提供证据或信息的来源，其中有些会公开，而你如果在代理一个群体，就可以援引它们。另一个很强的指标可以是

turns.en: if there is a parallel U.S. class action. That's another instance of sophisticated actors looking at this and coming to the same conclusion. And there can also be a fair bit of cross-border coordination and collaboration. If one of the lawsuits gets ahead of the other, let's say the Canadian lawsuit is ahead of the U.S. one, then you can share the evidence that comes to lighter the information that you get as long as it's not confidential. And you can share that and that can
turns.zh: 存在平行的美国集体诉讼：又一组精明的参与者看过之后得出同样的结论。而且跨境之间的协调与合作也相当多：如果一个官司跑在前面——比方说加拿大的诉讼在美国前面——那你们可以共享浮现出来的证据和获取的信息，只要不是保密的。你可以共享这些，而这能

turns.en: help drive some synergies between the two of them and can help push them along. Or vice versa, if the U.S. lawsuit is ahead of the Canadian lawsuit. In that type of scenario, how would it be determined in the asset management example that an asset manager has been a poor steward of their beneficiaries funds? I think a strong indicator is if they're filling to do what they say they're going to do, there's always some sort of statement out there about this is our investment thesis or
turns.zh: 推动两边产生协同、帮助两个案件互相前进；反过来也一样，如果美国诉讼走在加拿大诉讼前面。在这种情形下，在资产管理的例子里，怎么判断一个资产管理人没有管好受益人的钱、当了个糟糕的管家？我认为一个很强的迹象，就是他们做不到自己宣称要做的事。总有那么一份声明，说这是我们的投资理念，或者

turns.en: this is our approach. And if they start deviating from that, that's a problematic thing. That's a sign that something different is going on than what investors are being told. So that in and of itself doesn't necessarily mean that there have been losses, but it certainly is something that warrants fervor scrutiny if that comes to light. Beyond that, I think it's a very sort of individualized thing, but fees are another big indicator how fees are being charged. There have been a lot of class
turns.zh: 这是我们的方法。一旦他们开始偏离这套说法，那是个有问题的信号——说明实际发生的事情和投资者被告知的不一样。这本身未必意味着出现了亏损，但如果这一点浮出水面，绝对值得更严格的审视 (fervor scrutiny→更彻底的审查)。除此之外，我觉得这是非常个案化的事情，但费用是另一个大指标：费用是怎么收的。已经有很多与此相关的集体

turns.en: actions related to fees. There are certain fees that you can no longer charge them like they've explicitly changed the law. If let's say there was a fee that was being charged for advice and people were being charged that when they bought mutual fund units or what have you, even if it was a non-advice account, there were quite a few class actions over that digging under the hood and seeing what kinds of fees are being charged or how they're being calculated. I think that's
turns.zh: 诉讼。有些费用现在已经明令不能收了——法律明确改了。比如说，以前有些费用是以'建议费'名义在人们买共同基金份额时收取的，哪怕那是个非建议型账户 (non-advice account)，也因此引发了不少集体诉讼，去揭开盘子里面到底收的是什么费、怎么算的。我觉得那肯定是

turns.en: certainly an area where there's going to be a lot of litigation in the future. And I know we're going to talk about private assets later, but I think that's probably a particularly ripe area for private asset managers. Do class actions come up with pension funds often? They certainly do. So for the disclosure type class actions that I mentioned before, pension funds are very frequent litigants. They'll be the lead point of the representative point of law of the time. And
turns.zh: 未来会有大量诉讼的一个领域。我知道我们后面会谈私募资产，我觉得那对私募资产管理人来说可能是个特别成熟的诉讼领域。集体诉讼在养老基金里常见吗？当然常见。就我之前提到的信息披露型集体诉讼而言，养老基金是非常频繁的诉讼参与方，它们常担任首席原告 (lead plaintiff)。而在

turns.en: the United States, that genre of lawsuit, they actually changed the law for there to be an automatic presumption that the largest loser is the one that should get to leave the claim.
turns.zh: 美国，那一类诉讼的法律改了，现在自动推定损失最大的那家机构应该有资格担任首席原告。

turns.en: And when that happens, there is a lot more activity from pension funds in the United States. We don't have that rule explicitly in Canada, but I do think it's socialized a lot of the pension funds to the idea of participating in litigation, particularly the American pension funds, in a way that they wouldn't have before. Their involvement is pretty common at this point in time, but not universal. What about beneficiaries going after their own pension fund for how it's
turns.zh: 这条规则生效后，美国养老基金在那方面的活跃度高了很多。加拿大没有明文照搬这条规则，但我确实认为，它已经让很多养老基金——尤其是美国的——形成了参与诉讼的观念，而它们以前不会这样。到现在，它们的参与相当普遍，但并非无一例外。那受益人反过来起诉自家养老基金、质疑它是怎么被管理的，这种情况呢？

turns.en: been managed? So that is certainly a type of coin that can happen. There will be debates about how benefits are calculated or certain cutoff times or if it's an employment fund, whether or not different categories of employees of different kinds of claims, we do see those kinds of claims occasionally. They are not as common as the others that I mentioned, but they have happened and I am sure that there will be more of them in the future as well. For people who are in oversight
turns.zh: 这类事情确实会发生。围绕福利如何计算或某些截止时点会有争论；如果是与雇主相关的基金，不同类别员工是否有不同主张，也有争议。这类索赔我们偶尔会见到，虽然不如我提到的其他类型常见，但确实发生过，而且我确信未来还会有更多。对于那些在养老基金里担任监督

turns.en: roles on a pension fund, what do you think they should be aware of or looking out for as they monitor what their asset managers are doing? Obviously, there should be some degree of scrutiny and oversight of compliance, making sure that whether their state of investment goals are or their state of investment approach, so that's actually being adhered to. That's pretty basic and I would expect with pension funds because there's more oversight than for a lot of other
turns.zh: 岗位的人，你认为他们在监控资产管理人的作为时应该注意什么？显然，应该有一定程度的审查和监督：确认所声明的投资目标或投资方法是不是真的在被遵守。这是相当基本的要求，而且我认为养老基金在这方面本来就比很多其他

turns.en: asset managers. That's probably less of a concern. A related concern, I think, would be whether or not they're taking advantage of all of the money that's available to them through settlements.
turns.zh: 资产管理机构接受更多监督，所以这大概不算最大的隐忧。我觉得一个相关的隐忧是：他们是否充分利用了和解中所有唾手可得的资金。

turns.en: There is a article written in the Stanford Law Review about 20 years ago called, Letting Delian slip through your fingers in empirical evidence and legal implications of the failure of financial institutions to participate in securities class-action settlements, which is a mouthful. The basic thesis there was that at that point in time, there are quite a few pension funds or other asset managers that weren't participating in settlements and they're
turns.zh: 大约 20 年前，《斯坦福法律评论》(Stanford Law Review) 有篇文章，标题叫《让养老金从指缝间溜走：金融机构未参与证券集体诉讼和解的实证证据与法律后果》(Letting Pensions Slip Through Your Fingers)——名字很长。它的基本论点是：在当时，有不少养老基金和其他资产管理机构没有去参与和解，

turns.zh: 认为这是值得相关人员认真思考的审慎之举。当我们谈受托人标准 (fiduciary standard) 时，要知道：诉讼中的权益本身就是一项资产，它有价值、可以被出售。我们之前谈诉讼出资市场，那其实就是出售诉讼权益的一部分。至少在我看来，它就是一项需要像其他资产一样管理的资产，人们应该思考它、并对是否参与、

Now, if you had a fund, the whole thing was we're risk capital fund and we're looking for a junior gold mining company that we're going to 20X on and that's the purpose of this fund existing.
turns.zh: 我想问的是：对一个受益人分散的大型资产所有者来说，只买指数基金在法律上站得住脚吗？我认为这取决于他们声明的目标。如果某个基金从头到尾说的就是：我们是风险资本基金，要去找一家能涨 20 倍的初级金矿公司，这就是这个基金存在的目的——

turns.en: They'd be outside of their mandate by doing that. However, if it was a fund that had a more conservative kind of objective, then I don't see any issue with them basically having the entirety or most of their exposure to low-cost index funds as long as it's matching the risk profile that they are mandated to take on. I'm curious if you happen to have a favorite investing-related class action story. There have been a lot of interesting ones out there.
turns.zh: 那么他们买指数基金就超出了职责授权 (mandate)。但如果一个基金的目标本来就比较保守，我不觉得有什么大问题让他们把全部或大部分敞口放在低成本指数基金上，只要这与他们被授权承担的风险状况相匹配。我很好奇你有没有一个比较喜欢的投资相关的集体诉讼故事。市面上有很多有意思的案例。

turns.en: One of the more notorious ones would be Sinoforest, which was a TSX listed company that reported to have, I think, three-quarters of a million hectares of trees that they were going to harvest in China. turns.zh: 其中比较臭名昭著的一个是 Sino-Forest（加汉林业），一家在 TSX 上市的公司，据称在中国拥有大约 75 万公顷待采伐的林地。它巅峰时期的市值相当可观，有几十亿美元，年营收我记得大概十亿美元左右。

I think that's probably one of the more notable
turns.zh: 后来有欺诈调查，皇家骑警 (RCMP) 介入，安大略省证券委员会 (OSC) 介入，还有一场很大的集体诉讼。最后发现林子里根本没有树——起因是一份做空报告，做空者做了些背景调查，之后公司价值基本瞬间崩塌，进入破产程序，多人因欺诈被起诉。我觉得这大概是

turns.en: ones from my perspective, that a company reached a multi-billion dollar valuation based on possession of a forest in terms of there is no trees there.
turns.zh: 从我的视角看最值得铭记的案例之一：一家公司靠'拥有一片森林'达到几十亿美元的估值，而那里根本没有树。

turns.en: Wild. I think it was a $6 billion market cap at its peak. Yeah, that sounds about right to me. Pretty crazy. You mentioned this. I want to come back to private assets. What makes private assets problematic specifically for retail investors?
turns.zh: 太离谱了。我记得巅峰市值是 60 亿美元左右。差不多。真的很疯狂。你之前提到过这个，我想回到私募资产：私募资产对散户投资者来说，问题具体出在哪里？

turns.en: I think that there are two umbrella issues and they're related, but right off the bat, there's less information about these assets and there's less regulation, and both of those things are by design for better or worse. We've been talking a lot about information asymmetries and how that filters through all of this. There is always an information asymmetry when you're purchasing an investment product or shares in a company because management is always going to
turns.zh: 我觉得有两个伞状层面的问题，它们互相关联。首先，这类资产的信息更少、监管也更少——无论好坏，这两点都是制度设计使然。我们一直在谈信息不对称 (information asymmetry) 如何贯穿这一切。购买任何投资产品或公司股份时永远存在信息不对称，因为管理层懂得总比你多。

turns.en: know more than you do. That's just part of the separation of ownership and control, but if you're dealing with something in public markets, there are a lot of checks and balances meant to level that out to a pretty significant degree. There's regular disclosure of financials.
turns.zh: 这只是所有权与控制权分离的一部分。但如果你做的是公开市场，那里有很多制衡机制意在相当程度上拉平这种不对称：财务信息定期披露。

turns.en: There's audit of financials on a regular basis, so you are having a third party take a look and making sure this checks out. There's oversight to a degree, and there tends to be a greater amount of regulatory oversight as well. When you're dealing with these public market companies too, beyond the legal requirements, there are a lot of market actors that are private entities that follow these investments and they report on them. You've got equity analysts
turns.zh: 财务报表定期接受审计，也就是有第三方来核验是否说得通；有一定程度的监督，通常监管监督也更多。而且对这些公开市场公司，除了法律要求之外，还有很多私营的市场参与者跟踪并报道这些投资：股票分析师

turns.en: following most major listed companies, and what equity analysts are saying is going to get picked up by reporters. You can have the globe in mail. You can read about the latest quarterly from whatever your favorite TSX listed company is. There's a high level of interpretation of that information happening too. Your average person doesn't really know how to read financial statements from a public company, but they can probably figure out picking up the globe in mail and have a
turns.zh: 覆盖大多数主要上市公司，而股票分析师说了什么又会被记者报道。你可以看《环球邮报》(The Globe and Mail)，读到你最喜欢的那家 TSX 上市公司的最新季报。对这些信息的解读层次也很丰富。普通人未必看得懂上市公司的财务报表，但翻翻《环球邮报》，大概也能有个

turns.en: rudimentary idea of what's going on at least. Beyond the lessened information asymmetry, you've also got a lot of people whose job is to digest and disseminate this information too. That's stripped away by and large for private assets. The strict legal reporting requirements are very limited. You don't really have the same degree of sophisticated people like equities analysts that are reporting on them. The information that would be available to those people is going to
turns.zh: 至少初级的概念。在信息不对称被削弱之外，还有一大群人的工作就是消化并传播这些信息。而这一切对私募资产来说基本被剥掉了：严格法定披露要求非常有限，也没有同等程度的股票分析师这类专业人群在报道它们；即便有人想报道，能拿到的信息

turns.en: be a lot more limited to begin with. Beyond that, the structures that you're dealing with tend to be a lot more complex. When people think about investment products from my perspective or what I'm hearing is they usually think about a stalker bond and they go, okay, I own part of the company or I've made a loan to the company. I can understand in a rudimentary way what it is that I've got in my portfolio. One security is one company or they might think of it an ETF
turns.zh: 本来就少得多。除此之外，你面对的结构往往复杂得多。人们从我的视角——或者说我听到的——思考投资产品时，通常想的是一只股票或一只债券：好吧，我拥有公司的一部分，或者我借钱给了公司，我能粗略理解我组合里拿的是什么。一支证券对应一家公司；或者他们想到的是一只 ETF

turns.en: or a mutual fund and if it's a broad-based index type of product, they understand, okay, I've just got that a large scale. It's sliced and diced. I've got a tiny bit of a huge number of companies rather than a tiny bit of one company. They can get that at basic level at least. When you're dealing with a private asset, frequently what's being sold is more some form of a business strategy that they're going to do a roll-up of veterinary clinics. That's what this fund is going to be
turns.zh: 或一只共同基金，如果是宽基指数型产品，他们明白：我拿的是大规模的切分，是一大批公司各一点，而不是一家公司的一小份——起码这个层面能理解。但当涉及到私募资产时，被卖出的往往是某种商业策略：比如对连锁动物医院做连锁收购 (roll-up)，这只基金要做的就是

turns.en: where they've got a commercial real estate portfolio at a particular geographic location. What's kind of pernicious is that the investment thesis might sound very easy to understand, but if you look at what's actually under the hood, you might have five, six, seven different entities that are involved in managing this fund in different ways. You've got the people who are responsible for the actual capital and then they retain managers who aren't necessarily the individuals
turns.zh: 在某个特定地区持有一个商业地产组合。有点阴险的地方在于，投资理念听起来可能非常好理解，但你看实际盘子里有什么——管理这只基金的实体可能有五六个甚至七个，各自以不同方式参与。负责实际资本的是一批人，他们再聘请未必是同一批人的管理者，

turns.en: and then there might be property managers or there might be an management company for the veterinary clinics and they're all taking a fee. There's a lot of fees that are being paid out built into the structure in a way that's a lot more difficult to understand than an ETF fee that's 0.6% of the assets under management, but people feel like they can understand it and that can actually be a fairly dangerous thing, I think. A big piece of the difficulty is the price
turns.zh: 然后可能还有物业管理公司，或者动物医院的管理公司，每一层都在收费。结构里埋着大量费用，远比一只 ETF 按管理规模收 0.6% 更难理解——而人们自以为能理解，这其实可能是相当危险的。难处的很大一块在于定价的

turns.en: discovery element as well because for pricing you're beholden to the managers in a way that you're not for a public market product. Security, if it's well traded, there's very robust pricing information because the pricing is just based on people transacting at a given time, like that is the price. You can be pretty confident if you've got a large listed company or a fairly actively traded ETF. Here, what you've got is management valuing or retaining somebody to value the assets
turns.zh: 发现 (price discovery) 机制：定价方面，你在很大程度上受制于管理人，这在公开市场产品上不会发生。证券如果交易活跃，定价信息就非常可靠，因为价格就是人们在某一刻成交的结果——那就是价格。拿一家大型上市公司或交易活跃的 ETF，你可以很有信心。而在这里，你面对的是管理层自己估值、或委托他人去评估

turns.en: there under the hood and I'm like shares in your favorite big Canadian bank. If you've got a commercial loan portfolio, there's not an active market for that. If you've got a portfolio of veterinary clinics, there's not an active market for that, but the number of purchasers is pretty small and those deals are going to be much more kind of one-off deals. They're going to fairly complex terms versus I'm willing to buy this share for $50 a share. You want to sell a thousand shares,
turns.zh: 盘子里的资产。就像你最喜欢的加拿大大型银行的股票：一个商业贷款组合没有活跃市场；一堆动物医院的组合也没有活跃市场。潜在买家很少，交易更多是各种一次性的、条款相当复杂的买卖——而不是'我愿意每股 50 美元买，你想卖一千股，

turns.en: I'll pay you $50,000. That's pretty simple to understand, but the liquidity events that happen in a private asset are not at all comparable. You need some sort of a valuation metric to value these on an ongoing basis because the value is what affects the number of units people get when they purchase or when they redeem. You need regular valuation, but you don't have regular price information and that can open the door to quite a bit of mischief, I think. Related to that is the
turns.zh: 我就付你 5 万美元'这种简单理解的事。私募资产里发生的流动性事件完全不可比。你需要某种估值指标来持续评估，因为净值决定了人们申购和赎回时拿到的份额数量。你需要持续估值，却没有持续的价格信息——这扇之门一开，我觉得能生出不少猫腻。与此相关的还有

turns.en: way that fund managers get paid. The difficulty of returns is another problem for retail investors, I think. Again, coming back to the common share example, somebody buys a share at $20, they sell at $30, they realized a $10 profit, assuming there's no transaction costs. Everybody can understand that pretty easily. They go, okay, I realized a 50% return. Private assets tend to be a stream of returns that don't lend themselves to that calculation in the same way. There are different
turns.zh: 基金经理的收费方式。回报的难点对散户投资者也是另一个问题。还是拿普通股举例：某人 20 美元买入，30 美元卖出，实现 10 美元盈利——假设没有交易成本——所有人都能轻松理解：我赚了 50% 的回报。私募资产往往是一串回报流，没法用同样的方式做这种计算，

turns.en: metrics. One of the more commonly reported ones is internal rate of return, and that tries to give you a percent return accounting for the fact that it's a stream of payments rather than a single transaction return, and it gives you a percent. My belief is the average person looking at it goes, okay, I can compare this percent to what I would get on the common share example, and that's an apples to apples comparison. It's actually an apples to oranges comparison, and those two
turns.zh: 指标。比较常报告的是内部收益率 (internal rate of return, IRR)，它试图在承认这是一串现金流而非单笔交易回报的前提下，给你一个百分比。我的观察是：普通人看到这个百分比，会以为可以拿它和股票那个例子做 apples-to-apples 的比较，

turns.en: numbers do not necessarily square with one another very well at all. And there's an anchoring effect that's built into internal rate of return as well, where very early returns can significantly affect that number for years and years down the line. It's quite difficult for the average person to evaluate how their investment is performing when they're holding these compared to other investment products, and IRR is frequently what's setting the way that managers are being paid as
turns.zh: 数字彼此之间根本未必对得上。那实际是 apples-to-oranges 的比较。而且 IRR 内建了一种锚定效应 (anchoring effect)：很早发生的回报会在之后很多年持续扭曲这个数字。对普通人来说，持有这类资产时评估其表现，比其他投资产品困难得多，而 IRR 往往正是管理人付费的基准——

turns.en: well. So you've got this complex fee structure that's attached to this return metric that's difficult to follow, which is in turn rooted in this pricing information that is not market pricing like you've got with common shares, and all of those layers of complexity add upon one another, and they make it much more difficult for the average person to understand what they're holding, and somebody's recommending them. I think it's a lot more difficult for them to explain to their
turns.zh: 同样如此。于是你面对的是：一套复杂的收费结构，挂在难以追踪的回报指标上，而这个指标又建立在非市场定价的估值信息上——和普通股的市场价格完全不同——这些复杂性层层叠加，让普通人更难理解自己持有的到底是什么，也更难理解向他们推荐的人。我认为推荐人更难向

turns.en: client or have faith in their diligence in terms of the products that they're approaching the client with. I mentioned apples and oranges. There's a paper from Ludovic Falapu, who's been a guest on this podcast a while ago now. He does a lot of research on private equity in his 2026 paper, titled Apples and Oranges, Benchmarking Games and the Illusion of Private Equity Outperformance.
turns.zh: 客户解释清楚，也很难让人对他们的尽职调查有信心——就他们拿来见客户的那些产品而言。我刚才提到 apples and oranges。Ludovic Phalippou 有一篇论文——他早些时候来过我们这个播客——他对私募股权研究很深，2026 年这篇论文标题是《苹果与橙子：基准比较游戏与私募股权跑赢的幻觉》(Apples and Oranges: Benchmarking Games and the Illusion of Private Equity Outperformance)。

turns.en: Yeah, Ludovic is a very smart guy. Obviously, I don't have even attempt the understanding that he does, but I do think that sheds light on a lot of these issues.
turns.zh: 对，Ludovic 是个非常聪明的人。几个月前我在牛津时和他喝了杯咖啡，聊过这些话题。他关于这个主题的大部分论文我都读过，觉得非常有启发性。我的理解肯定远远比不上他，但我确实认为这些研究照亮了我们谈的很多问题。

turns.en: What additional steps should advisors recommending private assets be taking? Backing up, because this is related to what we're talking about, the liquidity problems that are inherent in these funds, I think should be front and center for advisors if they're going to be dealing with them. The liquidity piece of this is that basically all these funds can be gay, they're locked up. People don't necessarily understand that they won't be able to redeem
turns.zh: 推荐私募资产的顾问还应该多做些什么？先退一步说，因为这和我们一直在讨论的内容有关：这类基金固有的流动性问题，应该在顾问经手时处于最显眼的位置。流动性问题在于，基本上所有这些基金都可以被 gating（限制赎回）、被锁定。人们未必理解，自己不能

turns.en: their funds at any time, like they could with a mutual fund. Normally, you can redeem, you've got the money in your account within a day or two, it's a straightforward thing. People think, you know, I've got an emergency, I need to repair my house, my roof is gone bad, I need a new car, whatever, I can access that money. That's not the case with private funds, so that's another difficulty for clients to understand. I think it's an extremely important thing for advisors to be
turns.zh: 像赎回共同基金那样随时把钱取出来。通常共同基金你可以赎回，一两块钱就到账——很简单。人们会想：我有紧急情况，房子要修、屋顶坏了、要买新车，总之我能动用那笔钱。私募基金不是这样，这是客户要理解的又一个难点。我认为顾问有一件极其重要的事，就是

turns.en: talking to their clients about is understanding that there might be a mismatch between their liquidity needs at any given time and what these particular products can offer. I think warning of all of the risks that we've been talking about, all the risks that are structural to these products is a very important thing for the advisor if they're going to be recommending them and papering that they've actually taken the steps to warn them, gone through whatever compliance
turns.zh: 跟客户谈清楚：他们任何时点的流动性需求，和这些产品实际能提供的，两者之间可能存在错配。把我们一直在谈的所有风险——这些产品结构性内嵌的所有风险——向客户警示清楚，对打算推荐它们的顾问来说非常重要；而且要把警示真正做了的记录留痕：走完合规要求的

turns.en: steps they need to, and making sure that all their ducks are around that from would be very important. If you're helping to generate a plan for somebody, if it's not just investment selection or investment advice, I think it would be extremely important to ensure that that plan has contingencies in place for the event that anticipated cash flow coming from the private side of the portfolio is not available because gating is all over the news right now. I'm getting
turns.zh: 流程、确保各方环节都安排妥当——这非常要紧。如果你是在帮人做整体规划，而不只是挑选投资，我认为尤其重要的是确保这个规划预留了应变方案：万一私募端预期会来的现金流兑现不了怎么办。因为 gating 现在满屏新闻，我接到的

turns.en: more calls and I can count about gating. It is something that is happening right now and will probably be a feature for the foreseeable future to some degree, so counting for that in the plan would be a very important thing. I don't think you can take it as a given that the liquidity event is going to happen or the payments that we're supposed to happen are going to, so if it is going to be part of the portfolio, there needs to be some amount of planning going around what's going
turns.zh: 关于 gating 的问询越来越多，这是正在发生的事，而且在未来可预见的时期内大概仍会是常态的一部分，所以在规划里把它计算在内非常重要。你不能假定流动性事件一定会发生、该付的钱一定会付。所以如果私募要成为组合的一部分，就必须围绕'如果那些钱实际上取不出来该怎么办'做一些规划。

turns.en: to happen if those funds actually aren't available. Placing it within the context of the portfolio as a whole and making sure that it's appropriate, that's a very basic thing, but I think it's particularly important here because of the fact that you guys, somebody walked into a portfolio that could become inappropriate and you can actually really rebalance that in a meaningful way.
turns.zh: 如果那些钱实际上取不出来该怎么办，并且把它放在整个组合的背景下去审视、确认它是合适的——这是很基本的要求，但在这里尤其重要：因为你描述的处境是，一个人可能落入一个已经变得不合适的组合，而你实际上没办法有效地把它再平衡回来。

turns.en: There's a lot of knock-on effects that come from gating because people are essentially stuck with that position indefinitely. They're really at the mercy of the fund manager for the most part and can you build around that and get back to a suitable portfolio? Something does happen there.
turns.zh: gating 会带来很多连锁反应：人们基本上无限期地被困在那个仓位里，很大程度上只能任基金管理人摆布。还能围绕它做调整、回到一个合适的组合吗？这是真实存在的问题。

turns.en: That's a pretty important question that I think people would need to turn their mind to. Explaining the differences in returns and how to evaluate returns, explaining how fees are calculated, I think that's important as well because clients need to be going into this with their eyes open and actually understanding what it is that they're signing up for. The last one is usually these products are exempt market. They're sold through some sort of a prospectus
turns.zh: 我觉得这是个非常重要的问题，人们需要认真想一想。解释回报的差异、如何评估回报，解释费用怎么计算——我认为这也重要，因为客户需要睁着眼睛走进来，真正理解他们签的是什么。最后一点：这些产品通常是豁免市场 (exempt market) 产品，通过某种招募说明书

turns.en: exemption. It is on you to ensure that the client actually meets whatever exemption you're relying on. You need to be confident that their assets actually meet the requirements that they are able to legally purchase this product at all. Otherwise, that could cause problems for you down the line. What about from the client's perspective? If they're being recommended by an advisor to invest in private assets, what additional steps do you think the client should be taking?
turns.zh: 豁免 (prospectus exemption) 出售。确保客户确实符合你所援引的豁免条件，是你的责任。你必须确信他们的资产真的满足要求、在法律上本来就买得了这个产品，否则将来会给你自己惹出麻烦。那从客户的角度呢？如果顾问向他们推荐私募资产，你认为客户自己还应该多做哪些功课？

turns.en: I think that they should be asking a lot of questions about that. Part of it might be looking at what's the product shelf that the person has available to sell me. A lot of the majority of the consultations that I have, these are being sold through somebody who only has an exempt market license. That's really all that they've got available to them probably is some suite of these kinds of private asset products. If you come to somebody who is acting as more of a salesman,
turns.zh: 我觉得他们应该多问很多问题。其中一部分是看：这个人手上可以卖给我的产品货架 (product shelf) 是什么？我接到的大多数咨询里，这些东西是通过只有豁免市场牌照的人卖出来的——他们能卖的恐怕就是一整套这类私募资产产品。如果你遇到的是一位更像推销员的

turns.en: the advisor, they're going to try and sell you what they have. It's like going to a car dealership. You walk into a Ferrari dealership, they're going to try and sell you a Ferrari, even if maybe what you need is a Dodge Minivan, but they're going to try and make the pitch. They're going to try and deal what they've got. I think that people might want to know what is, what they can actually offer them. I'm not saying private assets are always inappropriate and people should never sell them,
turns.zh: 顾问，他们就会想办法把货架上有的东西卖给你。就像去汽车经销商：你走进 Ferrari 4S 店，他们会努力卖你一辆 Ferrari，哪怕你真正需要的是一辆 Dodge 小面包车——但他们会照样推销，就卖他们有的。我认为人们应该先搞清楚对方到底能提供什么。我不是说私募资产永远不合适、永远不该卖，

turns.en: but if it's the only thing in your portfolio, I think it's going to be a very exceptional circumstance. That's appropriate. That might be the situation you find yourself in if that's all the person you're speaking with can sell you. I think having an understanding of what kinds of solutions they can offer you would be a pretty important one before you're getting into this.
turns.zh: 但如果它是你组合里唯一的东西，那得是非常例外的情况下才是合适的。也许你之所以处于这种境地，是因为跟你谈的人只能卖给你这些。所以在入手之前，先理解对方能提供哪些解决方案，是相当重要的一课。

turns.en: If you've got a complex financial situation or you want exposure for some reason, if there's a percentage of your funds that you want invested in this for whatever reason, that can be a defensible thing. I can understand that as long as there's the discussion happening around it, it's not happening by default or just because that's all the person can offer you. I think understanding how the pieces fit together, having a conversation about how this is appropriate
turns.zh: 如果你的财务状况复杂，或者你出于某种原因想要这类敞口——想把一部分资金无论因由地投在这里——那可以是站得住脚的选择，我可以理解。前提是围绕它真的有充分讨论，而不是默认发生，也不是仅仅因为那是对方唯一拿得出手的东西。理解各部分如何拼合在一起，讨论它为什么适合你、

turns.en: and the context as a whole is a pretty important thing in doing your due diligence on the firm that you're working with, the person that's making these recommendations to you, ensuring that you really understand how this is going to help you meet your financial goals.
turns.zh: 以及放在整体背景下来看——这些都是尽职调查的重要环节：对你要合作的机构、给你出主意的人做好尽调，确保你真的理解它将如何帮你实现财务目标。

turns.en: So how do you think this push into private assets for retail investors will affect future litigation? I think that there's going to be a lot of litigation over this in the future.
turns.zh: 那么你怎么看这股面向散户的私募资产推广浪潮将如何影响未来诉讼？我认为未来围绕它会出现大量诉讼。

turns.en: We are starting to see more of it and part of that I think is if you look at the incentives to sue, all of this stuff can be reduced to incentives like most other things. Historically private assets were kind of the domain of the sophisticated entity. They were hedge funds, they might be some pension plans, whatever, they're very sophisticated entities. They're doing their own diligence in the way that the average person can't and they're going into it with their eyes
turns.zh: 我们已经开始看到更多苗头了。部分原因，我觉得是看起诉的激励——和大多数事情一样，这一切归根结底可以还原为激励问题。过去私募资产基本上是精明机构的领地：对冲基金，可能还有些养老金计划，都是非常老练的主体。他们以普通人做不到的方式自己做尽调，而且是睁大眼睛走进去的。

turns.en: open. Or beyond that, they wouldn't have incentives to sue because of the fact that some of the people that work at the fund might have an ongoing relationship, they don't want to sour that relationship. They're looking at is okay, this was a bad deal, but we've had good deals and we'll have good deals in the future. Some people might be looking at like I would like to work in private equity, so I don't want to be the person that pulls the trigger
turns.zh: 除此之外，他们也可能没有起诉的激励，因为基金里的一些人之间可能存在持续的合作关系，他们不想把关系搞僵。他们会权衡：这笔交易是糟糕，但我们做过好交易，将来还会有好交易。还有些人可能想的是：我以后想去私募股权行业工作，所以不想当那个扣扳机的人，

turns.en: on this and affects my own future career prospects. They go a lot of reasons not to sue in these situations and in particular in the US, binding arbitration has been something that's been forced upon them too. So if they are suing, it's not something that we're seeing. There are a few decisions where people have been forced into arbitration that are public by the courts.
turns.zh: 在这一点上提起诉讼、影响自己未来的职业前景。不起诉的理由很多。特别是在美国，强制性仲裁 (binding arbitration) 也被强加在他们头上。所以即便有人起诉，也不是我们常看到的景象。法院已有公开的少数裁决，认定投资者被强制推入了仲裁。

turns.en: So you can see that all of those considerations for the most part in Canada, if you're dealing with retail investors fall away, they probably don't care about their ongoing relationship with the fund manager. They're seeing this was a bad thing that happened and I ever want to do with this person again. I don't care if I sue them or not. I don't care if that's something that's going to affect this going forward. It's more difficult to force retail investors into arbitration
turns.zh: 所以你可以看到，在加拿大，对散户投资者而言，上述考量基本上统统不成立。他们大概不在乎与基金管理人的长期关系：他们看到的是这事坑了我，我再也不想和这个人有任何瓜葛。我起不起诉无所谓，会不会影响将来也无所谓。而在加拿大，把散户强制推入仲裁

turns.en: in Canada. Things like class action waivers are more difficult to enforce than the United States. All of these incentives align in all this context in a way that I think would make litigation much more likely and I think that we will see litigation over some of the issues that we've been talking about more and more frequently in the Canadian courts.
turns.zh: 要难得多。集体诉讼弃权条款 (class action waivers) 之类也比美国更难执行。所有激励、所有背景这样叠加在一起，我认为只会让诉讼更有可能发生。我们会越来越多地在加拿大法院看到围绕我们谈过的这些问题的诉讼。

turns.en: There's another paper from Ludovic and William Magnuson who actually has also been a guest in this podcast where they talk about, I think in a U.S. context, but they say, as a result, asset classes long confined to qualified investors are now being offered to the public but without the protection traditionally attached to public offerings.
turns.zh: Ludovic 和 William Magnuson 还有一篇论文——Magnuson 也来过我们这个播客——他们在（我想是美国语境下）写道：结果就是，长期只面向合格投资者 (qualified investors) 的资产类别，如今正被出售给公众，却不附带公开发行传统上应有的保护。

turns.en: This article argues that the retailization of private equity creates a significant regulatory gap. Practices normalized in institutional settings, misleading performance metrics, manipulatable valuations, opaque fees, limited liquidity, all stuff that you've talked about, and fiduciary duty waivers become significant litigation risks when ordinary investors enter the picture. I completely agree with that paper. I've read it and I lecture on this topic.
turns.zh: 这篇文章认为，私募股权的散户化 (retailization) 制造了一个重大监管缺口。那些在机构环境中被默认的做法——误导性的业绩指标、可被操纵的估值、不透明的费用、有限的流动性，全是你刚才讲过的东西——再加上受托义务的豁免，一旦普通投资者入场，就变成了重大的诉讼风险。我完全同意这篇论文。我读过它，而且我讲课也讲这个主题。

turns.en: That's part of the assigned readings that I give to people. A lot of what they've spoken about in that paper, it's even more true in the Canadian context. For instance, there's a section in the Securities Act that creates a right of action for people for misrepresentations and offering memoranda. A lot of the time offering memoranda will be part of the sales pitch for these products. What people think they're buying into doesn't necessarily match what's under the
turns.zh: 那是我给学生开的指定阅读材料之一。他们论文里讲的许多现象，在加拿大语境下甚至更甚。举个例子，《证券法》(Securities Act) 里有一条款，为认购文件 (offering memorandum) 中的虚假陈述创设了诉权。很多时候，认购文件本来就是这些产品销售话术的一部分。而人们以为自己要买的东西，未必和盘子里实际装的相符——

turns.en: hood. It's explicitly part of Ontario legislation that you can sue for that mismatch. I think their retail investor will be much more likely to do that. Man, we've stayed away from private assets, probably speaking. I want to move on to the final topic we have questions on, which is influencers or financial influencers. Can you talk about the legal and regulatory challenges that influencers pose? I think they pose a lot of difficulties, and part of the problem is
turns.zh: 安大略省的成文法明确允许就这种不符提起诉讼。我认为散户投资者会更可能这么做。天哪，我们在私募资产上聊了很久了。我想转到最后一个我们准备了问题的主题：网红，或者说金融网红 (finfluencer)。能谈谈网红带来的法律和监管挑战吗？我认为他们造成很多困难，其中一部分问题在于——

turns.en: even knowing who's going to deal with them. That's the first point that we come into for a regulator from a regulatory perspective. Video is everywhere. Audio is everywhere. We could have listeners when we're done this. Australia, South Africa, wherever. If there's a problem, who's going to address that problem? That's sort of question number one. If you're dealing with a more bread and butter market misconduct type of issue, it's pretty obvious
turns.zh: 甚至不知道该由谁来管他们。这是站在监管角度遇到的第一道题。视频无处不在，音频无处不在。等我们这期说完，听众可能在澳大利亚、南非、任何地方。如果出了问题，谁来处理？这是第一号问题。如果是比较常规的市场不当行为 (market misconduct) 问题，那很清楚：

turns.en: somebody is hogging products out of their office and mark them or bury or wherever. You know, okay, we're dealing with the Ontario Securities Commission. Even within Canada, each province has their own commission. If you've got somebody who's recording this content in Manitoba relating to an Alberta company and their transactions happening in Ontario, people need to figure out, hey, who's going to try and deal with this problem? The different commissions can and do
turns.zh: 有人窝在自己办公室里囤积产品、抢跑交易 (front run) 或埋单之类的，你知道，那就是归安大略省证券委员会 (OSC) 管。即便在加拿大国内，每个省也有自己的委员会。如果有人在马尼托巴省录制内容，谈论一家阿尔伯塔省的公司，交易却发生在安大略省——人们就得先搞清楚：嘿，谁来处理这个问题？各个委员会之间

turns.en: coordinate, but immediately off the bat, you've got, okay, this is a problem waiting to think about it, and that's without even dealing with the cross-border or transnational aspects of it.
turns.zh: 确实会协调、也确实在协调，但从一开始这就是个'还没人认领'的问题——而这甚至还没碰跨境和跨国层面。

turns.en: Another issue is private enforcement incentives are limited. And why say private enforcement? I mean lawsuits. So, somebody relies on this bad advice. The incentives to sue are less because of the fact that you don't need to have insurance as a fence loan. So, anybody can make a podcast, anybody can plug in a mic, they can serve recording, they can say whatever they want, and they can pretty easily reach other wide audience over, pick your favorite video platform,
turns.zh: 另一个问题是私人执法 (private enforcement) 的激励有限。我说私人执法，意思就是打官司。如果有人依赖了糟糕的建议——起诉的动力比较低，原因之一是像无保险垫底这类问题：谁都能做播客，谁都能插上麦克风开始录制，想说什么都行，而且随便挑一个你最喜欢的视频平台

turns.en: audio streaming platform. Most people can find a way on there, particularly if they've got a listener base. But that doesn't mean that there's actually going to be a reason to sue them in terms of getting your money back if you follow bad advice, because they might be completely broke. There's been a few prosecutions of influencers by regulators in Canada, and they've actually accounted for the fact that the person has no or very limited assets in the fines that
turns.zh: 或音频流媒体平台，就能相当轻松地触达很宽的受众。大多数人总能找到露面的路子，尤其当他们已有听众基础时。但如果你听了坏建议亏了钱，想让起诉有实际意义——把本金追回来——未必做得到，因为他们可能一贫如洗。加拿大已经有监管方起诉网红的若干案例，而最终裁定的罚款里，其实已经把当事人没有资产或资产极有限这一事实考虑了进去。

turns.en: they ultimately levy. For the average person looking to do this, the first pair of the conversation is always, can we actually even get you any money back, or are you going to be throwing good money after bad by engaging a lawyer and trying to do this? Regulators have a bit more of a headache off the top. There's less incentive for the investor themselves to do something.
turns.zh: 对想维权的普通人来说，对话的第一部分永远是：我们到底能不能帮你拿回任何钱？还是说请律师这么折腾，只是往损失里再扔好钱？监管方从一开始也颇感头疼；投资者自己采取行动的动力更低。

turns.en: And you also get into this question of why amounts to advice. It can be very difficult to ascertain the financial relationships between a influencer and different companies or different entities because of the fact that, probably speaking, they're not really regulated.
turns.zh: 而且你还会碰到'什么构成建议'这个问题。要查清金融网红与不同公司或不同实体之间的财务关系可能非常困难，原因大概就是：总体上说，他们其实没怎么被监管。

turns.en: They're supposed to be regulated. If you're engaging in promotional activity, you're supposed to make disclosure, you're supposed to engage with the regulators. But there's so much of this going on right now, and regulators are everywhere, stretched pretty thin by a lot of internet related problems. It's not realistic for them to police 100% of this activity 100% of the time.
turns.zh: 按理他们该被监管：如果你从事推介活动 (promotional activity)，你就应该披露，应该配合监管机构。但现在这类活动太多了，而监管机构本来就被各种互联网相关的问题压得捉襟见肘。要求他们百分之百地管控百分之百的活动，不现实。

turns.en: So there's a lot of structural difficulties that come up with the Finfluencer type activity from pretty much every perspective that we expect to normally rein in a lot of regulatory issues.
turns.zh: 所以金融网红 (finfluencer) 这类活动，几乎从我们通常指望其约束监管问题的每个角度看，都存在大量结构性困难。

turns.en: How do you think investors should assess the credibility of a Finfluencer? I think that's a tough one, and going to a trusted source of advice is again, I think an important thing that they can do. But just looking at it, I think you always want to be thinking about why the person is making the particular recommendations they're making.
turns.zh: 你认为投资者应该如何评估一个金融网红的可信度？我觉得这很难。Again，转向一个可信赖的建议来源，我认为依然是他们能做的要事。但就说直接观察本身：我觉得你始终要思考——这个人为什么会给出他正在给出的具体推荐。

turns.en: If there's any kind of disclosure of a relationship, obviously, that's something that you will want to account for. And that's part of what should be happening with promotional activities, as if there is a relationship, it should be disclosed. From there, I think it's pretty hard.
turns.zh: 如果有任何形式的关系披露，显然那是你需要纳入考量的因素，这本来也是推介活动应当做到的：如果存在关系，就应当披露。在那之后，我觉得就很难办了。

turns.en: It's the wild west, frankly, there isn't a lot of good resources in terms of how people can familiarize themselves. They can do things like see if there has been any kind of regulatory action involving them. Google will pick that kind of thing up now. But in terms of diligence, we've got this information asymmetry problem that I've been coming back to a lot. And a lot of the time people are turning to a Finfluencer because they don't have access to your trusted
turns.zh: 坦白说那就是西部荒野 (wild west)，在帮助人们自我武装知识方面没有多少好资源。你能做的事之一，是看看有没有监管机构对他们采取过行动——如今谷歌搜得到这类信息。但在尽调层面，我们面对的还是我反复提到的那个信息不对称问题。很多时候人们转向金融网红，正是因为他们接触不到可信赖的建议

turns.en: source of advice. So it is self-selecting in a way too, which is part of why I think the educational component that professionals can have is a very important part of this.
